properties.description:

Hawk Channel and Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile
Bridge to Halfmoon Shoal out 60 nm...

At 741 PM EDT, National Weather Service meteorologists detected a a
strong thunderstorm, capable of producing wind gusts near 30 knots.
This thunderstorm was located near American Shoal Light, moving
southwest at 10 knots.

The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for thunderstorms with wind gusts near 30 knots, locally
rough and confused seas, occasional lightning strikes, and
potentially blinding downpours. Get to a safe port as quickly, and as
safely as possible. When downpours reduce visibility, slow down.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Clark County in southern Nevada, including
Valley of Fire State Park...

* WHEN...Until 700 PM PDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 405 PM PDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.25 and 0.75 inches of
rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Overton and Valley Of Fire.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by midweek. This trough should remain
strong and active while over the territory, and may even intensify
with embedded low pressure centers. Widespread showers may be
heavy and persistent at times with the possibility of
thunderstorms. Widespread flash flooding may occur from this
rainfall, and landslides will be possible along steep mountainous
terrain. Impacts could begin as early as Wednesday and are
expected to persist through the weekend. While there is still
uncertainty in the exact magnitude and duration of rainfall, plan
now for wet conditions that could start as early as Wednesday and
persist through at least Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our
internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 12 at 10:39AM EDT by NWS Marquette MI
properties.description:
The Michigan Department of Environmental Quality has issued an Air
Quality Alert for Monday October 12, for elevated levels of
fine particulates (PM2.5) due to wildfire smoke. Localized pollutants
levels within those area may reach the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups with the the potential for Unhealthy.

The alert is in effect for the following Michigan Counties,

Menominee, Dickinson, Iron, Marquette, and Baraga.

It is recommended that, when possible, you avoid strenuous outdoor
activities, especially those with heart disease and respiratory
diseases such as asthma.

Monitor for symptoms such as wheezing, coughing, chest tightness,
dizziness, or burning in nose, throat, and eyes. Reduce or eliminate
activities that contribute to air pollution, such as outdoor
burning, and use of residential wood burning devices.

Keep windows closed overnight to prevent smoke from getting indoors
and, if possible, run central air conditioning with MERV-13 or
higher rated filters.

For further information, please see EPA's Air Now site for up-to-
date air quality data at https://www.airnow.gov

For further health information, please see MDHHS' Wildfire Smoke and
Your Health site at https://www.michigan.gov/mdhhs/safety-injury-
prev/environmental-health/your-health-and-wildfire-smoke.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 12 at 1:29PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
As Invest 96W continues to slowly organize and strengthen north of
Kosrae/east of Pohnpei, inflow into the developing disturbance will
allow for locally heavy rainfall to develop, with over 1 inch per
hour rain rates probable from time to time. Rainfall totals will
likely be 2 to 5 inches tonight through Wednesday, with locally
higher amounts possible.

Winds will also increase as 96W strengthens, and at least isolated
wind gusts to 35 knots are possible with any heavy shower or
thunderstorm that develops.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island
boating as the week continues. Also keep up to date with the latest
information from your local emergency management agency.
